programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo travels to Uttoxeter from Liverpool, beginning by learning about the design of the city's Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King, inaugurated in 1967. programme.title: Walking with Jim Moir
programme.desc: The comedian better known to some as Vic Reeves explores a fascinating corner of the Kent coast as he walks down to Dungeness. Along the way he meets locals, explores military ruins and rides a steam train

programme.title: The Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the artistic achievements of the Romans, tracing their progression from thieves and copycats to pioneers of the use of unflinching realism. Portraits from the Republic reveal how they captured lifelike images and immortalised figures such as Julius Caesar and Cicero using marble, bronze and paint. Alastair also looks at how Rome's first emperor, Augustus, used art as a tool to forge his dominion

programme.title: Caligula with Mary Beard
programme.desc: Roman emperor Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus - better known as Caligula - was said to have made his horse a consul, proclaimed himself a living God and indulged in scandalous orgies. In this documentary, classical scholar Mary Beard attempts to peel away some of the myths surrounding him, sifting through surviving evidence to paint a portrait of the real Caligula

programme.title: Sir Derek Jacobi Remembers - I, Claudius

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Acclaimed drama set amidst a web of power, corruption and lies, chronicling the reigns of the Roman emperors - Augustus, Tiberius, Caligula and finally Claudius - focusing on the intrigue that surrounded their respective reigns. Augustus's wife Livia schemes to ensure her son Tiberius succeeds her husband. The dispute between Marcus Agrippa and Marcellus reaches boiling point, prompting the former to leave Rome for the East. With Derek Jacobi, Sian Phillips, Brian Blessed and George Baker

programme.title: I, Claudius

programme.title: Sally Magnusson Remembers - Mastermind
programme.desc: Broadcaster and writer Sally Magnusson takes her seat in the original, imposing 'Mastermind' chair, and shares her memories of her father Magnus' time as the host of one of British television's most enduring quiz shows. She tells the story of how the programme originated, how her father got the job of quiz master, and what it was like growing up as a teenager and having the catchphrases 'pass' and 'I've started, so I'll finish' hurled her way on a regular basis. Sally also reveals how it feels to sit and face questions in the famous chair, and how it came to be that it now lives in her own living room

programme.title: Trusadh (Compelling Stories)
programme.desc: Following a year in the life of student and Gaelic learner Loretta Crinall, as she leaves her home in Glasgow and makes her way to the largest city in South America, Sao Paulo, as part of her languages degree. Having recently left her career as a drag performer, Loretta is now embarking on a journey to an unknown country with all the challenges that come with it. As a minority language scholar and activist, this trip gives her the opportunity to conduct in-depth research on the regions indigenous people. On the Jaragua Mountain, on the outskirts of Sao Paulo, she meets the Guarani people who have lived there for centuries. In a conversation with Anthony Karai Poty, Loretta hears how the Guarani have fought to defend their way of life against violence and ignorance. This journey also gives Loretta the opportunity to look back on her life growing up as a black, trans woman, and the impact that has had on her, both personally and politically

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year 2024
programme.desc: Judges Anna Campbell-Jones, Banjo Beale and Danny Campbell visit properties in central Scotland. The first home for the judges to visit is the Old Mill near Dunblane, an empty industrial building converted a five-bedroom home. Next up is Sandstone Villa in Bridge of Allan, a semi-deteched property which dates back to the early 1900s. Finally, the judges visit Courtyard Farmhouse, a conversion of a once-derelict farmhouse between Falkirk and Linlithgow

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: Area operations manager Fiona Galbraith travels to Stornoway from her home on Benbecula to help out with a freight backlog and keep the essential supply lines open between the mainland and the Outer Hebrides. Sisters Natalie and Tanya Mackay from the Isle of Lewis are now a couple of weeks into their modern apprenticeship with CalMac and are about to join a vessel for the first time

programme.title: Mhairi Black: Being Me Again
programme.desc: The ex-SNP MP talks about her life in depth. As well as interviews with her wife Katie, and father Alan, cameras gain access at the House of Commons, and the first night of her stand-up show, Politics Isn't for Me, at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Mhairi, the youngest person elected to the House of Commons, also discusses feelings about her own neurodivergence

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Roisin is at her wits end when she reaches breaking point over Gillian's behaviour and Jodie drops a bombshell. Chris is forced to face the music when he realises paying Nicole is impossible, Tyler struggles to get dirt on Alex, and Amber considers her next steps with Angus

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: After accidentally picking up one of Cathy's novels, Agnes discovers she has a surprising fondness for steamy fiction. She then gatecrashes the next group meeting of Cathy's book group to share her insights on the genre, - mortifying her daughter in the process. Comedy, co-written by and starring Brendan O'Carroll, with Jennifer Gibney

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist explores how if a killer wants to get away with murder, they must get rid of the evidence - in other words, their victim - and their attempts to do that

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: Fifer Mathew, his girlfriend Alexandra, little brother Malachi and mum Amanda from Fife visit a selection of getaways steeped in history, staying at a retreat with a military past, a 500-year-old castle and a former train station hotel. JJ Chalmers and Grado present

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat, where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based crewmates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered a severe anaphylactic attack, but she shows little sign of improvement after several doses of adrenaline, prompting a rapid journey on blue-lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

programme.title: Rikki
programme.desc: Ashley Jensen narrates a programme celebrating the life, career and legacy of Rikki Fulton, one of Scotland's most beloved comic actors and undisputed King of Hogmanay. This film tells the story of his extraordinary life by bringing together the people closest to him and the people he inspired, with never-before-seen home movie footage and clips of the best-loved moments of his career

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Jack and Victor start to feel their age, but a new wonder drug promises to unlock the secret of eternal youth for the doughty pensioners. Comedy, starring Ford Kiernan and Greg Hemphill

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Cathy and Colin are back from an Italian holiday and excited to be hosting a soiree at their house - arranged for the purpose of showing off how popular they are. They invite Gail and Andy, who they met in Sorrento, but as the duty-free wine flows and the guests of honour begin to bond a bit too much with the neighbours, Cathy and Colin's tensions soon bubble to the surface

programme.title: Rip It Up
programme.desc: A look at how Scotland experienced a pop resurgence in the 1980s as bands such as Wet Wet Wet, Deacon Blue, Texas and the Proclaimers began to hit the charts. Contributors include Jim Kerr, Alan Rankine, Emma Pollock Martin Bulloch, Stuart Braithwaite, Dougie Vipond, Ricky Ross, Charlie and Craig Reid, Sharleen Spiteri , KT Tunstall, Duglas Stewart, Sean Dickson and Alan McGee

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: With Derek's retirement imminent, the Thomsons thrash out plans for Nick to take over the family farm. The Imrie family prepares to co-host a gourmet dining event featuring their homegrown lamb, but a storm threatens proceedings. In Caithness, Sally takes her four-year-old to market to sell his first ever lambs along with 20 of her own

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: The team plans for winter, with Ruth Vichos demonstrating how to cultivate and multiply snowdrops and Calum Clunie collecting seeds from this year's lupin to sow for future colour. Ruth is in her strawberry bed discussing how to get the most from your crop, and shows off some the country's favourite garden plants that she has in her competition plot

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Crews are mobilised to a large building fire in Glasgow city centre, with concerns that people are trapped inside. As fire and rescue battle the blaze, Stewart of the Paramedic Response Unit endures heavy rain and prepares to treat casualties. Meanwhile, Ayr-based crew Sophie and Shelby treat a man who has been drinking alcohol and has sustained a concerning head injury, but is adamant he doesn't want to go to hospital.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond focus on wild food, cooking gnocchi with smoked haddock and wild greens, with chef Billy Boyter and crime writer Val McDermid

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The summer months bring new opportunities and challenges for the people who work at the ski resort in the Cairngorms National Park. The funicular train comes off its tracks, Ruari the ski patroller turns gamekeeper for the summer, the new boss at the sailing school has big boots to fill and a young couple try to get their music festival off the ground

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: Spud the piper returns and has a riding lesson, Ruari goes diving for items on his wedding menu, the oldest ski tow on the mountain needs demolishing and a young biker gets out of school to go racing

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The team travel to the Royal Navy Air Station in Yeovilton, Somerset, where they are recruited to transform the communal spaces - officially known as mess decks - used by the new recruits for socialising, eating and relaxing. The six designers are given a room each and Michelle Ogundehin's brief is to create spaces that are practical and comfortable, to provide an escape from the regimented daily routine of life on the air station - and it isn't long before the beige walls and boring tables are being replaced by something much more colourful. What will Michelle and guest judge Kelly Holmes - who spent 10 years in the military herself - make of the changes?

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A guilt-ridden Conor tries to convince Nicole they should come clean. Having hit a wall to access Harry's fortune, Alex turns to an incredulous Lenny for help, Dean stands up to Callum and Shak, and Gillian is left devastated after meeting with DCI Douglas

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Colin turns to his neighbours for support when he is unceremoniously dumped by Cathy. Beth and Eric do their best to cheer him up, but conversation is already strained when Christine turns up and demands all of the juicy details from the break up. Later, Ian and Gordon arrive to share some good news, and together the neighbours try their best to make Colin feel positive about his future as a single man

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Discussion on Scotland's biggest news stories, with Martin Geissler, Laura Miller and Natalie Higgins

programme.title: Gary: Tank Commander
programme.desc: Gary swaps the tank for a Green Goddess as the army covers a firefighter strike. The boys prepare for their first blaze, but when it finally happens it is their people skills that face the ultimate test. Comedy, written by and starring Greg McHugh

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall presents some of his favourite moments from the wildlife series, including abseiling into the Gomantong cave system and meeting a hippo

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and his team show how they coped with filming in temperatures below minus 20 in the frozen tundra of Alaska and in the humidity and heat of the unforgiving rainforests of Brazil in order to capture the wildlife that call these places home

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May try to make train travel cheaper, faster and more interesting, replacing the locomotive with a specially modified car and the carriages with a series of caravans. Comedy star Rowan Atkinson gets behind the wheel of the Reasonably Priced Car and Jeremy drives the Jaguar XKR-S and a Nissan GT-R round the track to compare both models

programme.title: I Am Legend
programme.desc: A Manhattan-based military scientist finds himself immune to a virus that turns humans into ferocious vampire-like creatures. After the disease has swept across the world, wiping out an estimated 90 per cent of the human population, he devotes his solitary existence to finding a cure by unlocking the secret within his blood. Sci-fi thriller, starring Will Smith, Alice Braga and Charlie Tahan

programme.title: Kidnapped by My Mum
programme.desc: Part one of two. The story of Alex Batty, who went missing when he was 11 on what was supposed to be a short family holiday with his mother and grandfather. Now aged 20, he tells the full story about his abduction and his life on the run, retracing the route of his disappearance across Spain and France, uncovering not just how he was hidden but the belief system that kept him there

programme.title: Stacey Dooley: Ready for War?
programme.desc: The reporter follows a group of Ukrainian civilians as they arrive in the UK for five weeks of intensive army training before deployment to the frontline fighting against Russia. Among the group is florist and gardener Mykola who wants to join his family members on the frontline and fight towards victory so he can marry his girlfriend. For Pasha, a welder who was living abroad when the invasion began, he fears going into battle means never seeing his parents again

programme.title: Roman Kemp: The Fight for Young Lives
programme.desc: Broadcaster Roman Kemp knows first-hand the impact of serious mental health issues. In 2020, he made Our Silent Emergency in the wake of the death of a friend. He encouraged those in need to talk to friends, family and professionals, but now strives to move the conversation on from talking about mental health to discovering what action is needed to support those suffering

programme.title: Deadly 60

programme.title: Night at the Museum
programme.desc: A new nightwatchman at New York's Museum of Natural History discovers his job entails more than he bargained for. Once night falls, an ancient Egyptian spell brings the museum exhibits to life, entangling him in a riotous struggle to restore peace and order before the sun rises and visitors arrive. Fantasy comedy, starring Ben Stiller, Dick Van Dyke, Robin Williams, Carla Gugino and Ricky Gervais

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: The hunt for James takes a backseat as Lucy becomes embroiled in a murder plot and John desperately tries to prove her innocence. John becomes angry at his brother for abandoning his family and Lucy admits that what she really needs right now is Ludwig

programme.title: Ghosts Australia
programme.desc: When city couple Kate and Sean inherit a run-down country estate, they see it as a sign for a fresh start. But after Kate has a near-death experience, she gains the ability to see and hear ghosts, discovering there are several living in the mansion. Remake of the supernatural sitcom, starring Tamala Shelton and Rowan Witt

programme.title: Ghosts Australia
programme.desc: Kate has a hospital visit which only makes her more convinced of what she is seeing, and accepts that the ghosts are real

programme.title: Ghosts Australia

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: A counselling session elicits an uncomfortable truth from Fleabag and she finds herself somewhere unexpected. Meanwhile, a chat with her sister brings some unwelcome news, Fleabag faces off with her brother-in-law Martin, and Jake wonders where Claire is. Comedy written by and starring Phoebe Waller-Bridge, with Sian Clifford and Brett Gelman

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: An event at Claire's work sees Fleabag's efforts to help out inevitably end in disaster, but an introduction to one of her sister's colleagues proves intriguing, while a chance meeting with a stranger is an eye-opener. Comedy written by and starring Phoebe Waller-Bridge as a woman wrestling with the demands of modern living as she spins through London grasping at anyone and anything that might keep her head above water. programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: The Priest takes Fleabag for some quiet reflection, leading to an unexpected revelation. After a day spent looking back on painful memories, she turns to him for solace, only to find more trouble. Comedy written by and starring Phoebe Waller-Bridge, with Andrew Scott

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: Claire has a crisis and turns to Fleabag for help, while a familiar face makes a reappearance at the cafe. Comedy written by and starring Phoebe Waller-Bridge as a woman wrestling with the demands of modern living as she spins through London grasping at anyone and anything that might keep her head above water. Comedy written by and starring Phoebe Waller-Bridge as a woman wrestling with the demands of modern living as she spins through London grasping at anyone and anything that might keep her head above water. programme.desc: It is the day of Derrick and Yasuko's wedding, but Moz has a tough time getting the groom to the register officer on time. programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: PC warns Moz of an imminent drugs bust, so the dealer embarks on an unscheduled spring-cleaning exercise as he sets out to destroy all the evidence in his flat. Meanwhile, Colin falls in love, and Nicki goes into labour. Comedy, starring Johnny Vegas, Tom Goodman-Hill and Ben Crompton

programme.title: Ideal

programme.desc: Steve Backshall explores the wildlife of British Columbia, Canada. A search for a particularly large sea lion results in an unexpected encounter with a killer whale, and the naturalist tries his hand at becoming a raccoon in Vancouver

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Part one of two. Steve Backshall and the team travel to Costa Rica on a mission to find the jaguar, the largest cat in South America. They also encounter other wildlife in the rainforest, including deadly snakes and squealing frogs

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The amateur sewers tackle the fast fashion industry in reduce, reuse and recycle week, with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. They begin by making three pairs of knickers from old T-shirts - a task that tests both their technical skills and their consistency. They then use various waste items, from baubles to bike tyres, to help decorate their transformations, before creating made-to-measure outfits with an environmental message

programme.title: Top Gear Patagonia Special
programme.desc: The first half of a two-part special, the filming of which caused controversy in Argentina because of a registration plate that drew links to the Falklands War. Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May take three used V8-engined sports cars on a gruelling road trip covering 1,600 miles through Patagonia. Their chosen vehicles are the Porsche 928, Lotus Esprit and Ford Mustang, which are subjected to rigours beyond the scope of their original designs - from tackling swamps and crossing deserts to navigating forests, beaches and ski slopes. Their destination is Ushuaia, the world's southernmost city, where they hope to stage a game of car football against Argentina

programme.title: Top Gear Patagonia Special
programme.desc: The conclusion of the two-part special in which Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May take three used, V8-engined sports cars on a gruelling road trip covering 1,600 miles through Patagonia to the world's southernmost city. Having encountered stunning landscapes, mechanical mishaps and dreadful roads on their journey through Argentina, the trio's adventure is brought to a dramatic climax by a terrifying turn of events

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Following Hearts and Scotland goalkeeper Craig Gordon over the course of 12 months as he makes one last attempt to reach a World Cup. To get there, he has to overcome opposition on the pitch as well as the limitations of his own body as he battles injuries to keep the dream alive

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Documentary following boxer Tommy Fury's return to the ring. programme.desc: The Washington DC Open. Coverage of day three of the WTA 500 and ATP 500 event, a hard-court tournament held at William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center in the USA. All three of the British players involved in the second round of last year's competition emerged victorious, with Emma Raducanu beating four-time Grand slam champion Naomi Osaka in straight sets, while Dan Evans triumphed 6-4 6-4 over Alex Michelsen, and Cameron Norrie beat the number two seed Lorenzo Musetti 3-6 6-2 6-3. Perhaps the most notable victory was claimed by 2021 US Open runner-up Leylah Fernandez, who eliminated the number one seed Jessica Pegula in a see-saw encounter that finished 6-3 1-6 7-5 in her favour

All four the women's quarter-finals 12 months ago were settled in straight sets, with notable wins for 2021 US Open champion Emma Raducanu, who beat Maria Sakkari 6-4 7-5, while the woman she beat in that memorable final, Leylah Fernandez, triumphed 6-4 7-6 over Taylor Townsend. Four of the eight men's quarter-finalists last year were American, but only one of them progressed to the semi-finals, with Ben Shelton winning 7-6 6-4 against his compatriot Frances Tiafoe

Today will see the conclusion of the first round in both competitions, with players hoping to avoid elimination at the first step. Jacob Fearnley was the only British male involved at this stage last year, and suffered an early exit following a 2-6 3-6 loss to Argentinean qualifier Juan Pablo Ficovich. There were mixed fortunes for British representation in the women's competition, with Emma Raducanu booking her place in round two with a 6-2 6-4 win over Elena-Gabriela Ruse, but Katie Boulter was knocked out at the first time of asking as she lost 1-6 5-7 to Renata Zaraza
